claims.statement: An API key never lives in the renderer: LlmConfig has no apiKey field; the desktop app holds the key in the Electron main process encrypted with safeStorage, splices it into outgoing requests there, and the renderer only ever sees hasKey.

The renderer builds the entire LLM request but can only place the literal sentinel API_KEY_SENTINEL ('{{apiKey}}') where the key goes; the main process substitutes the real key by replacing the sentinel across every header value just before sending.

There are nine providers (anthropic, openai, google, openrouter, groq, mistral, deepseek, xai, openai-compatible); only openai-compatible has an editable base URL, and only openai-compatible has supportsModelListing false (no safe endpoint/shape to assume for an arbitrary self-hosted server).

supportsPdf is false for groq, mistral, deepseek, xai, and openai-compatible (no single inline-attachment request), so a target set to send the PDF against them silently falls back to extracted text at run time.

Each provider carries a tokenParam of 'max_tokens' or 'max_completion_tokens' to avoid the OpenAI-specific rename trap: OpenAI/Groq/xAI require max_completion_tokens on newer models while OpenRouter/Mistral/DeepSeek/self-hosted servers still use max_tokens; sending the wrong one fails the call.

buildRequest produces three genuinely different request shapes: Anthropic (POST /v1/messages, x-api-key, body with max_tokens/system/messages), Google (model in URL path, x-goog-api-key, generateContent body), and OpenAI-shaped (POST /v1/chat/completions, Bearer auth, the provider's tokenParam).

For Google, reasoning effort switches between thinkingLevel (named, Gemini 3.x via googleThinkingMechanism) and thinkingBudget (a token count derived from the chosen level via GOOGLE_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL, Gemini 2.5.x); the two are mutually exclusive and sending both is an error.
Reasoning effort for OpenAI-shaped providers is sent as reasoning_effort (flat) for all except OpenRouter, which takes { reasoning: { effort } } (nested).

DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS is deliberately generous (8192) because on reasoning-capable models the output budget is shared between hidden reasoning tokens and the visible answer; reasoning can exhaust the whole budget before any visible token is written, surfacing as a truncation flag with no usable text rather than an error.

Provider response reading is deliberately tolerant: extractText degrades to '' and extractError always yields something readable; wasTruncated distinguishes a 2xx response cut off by the token budget from the model having nothing to say, letting the store give a targeted 'budget exhausted on reasoning' message instead of 'the reply was empty'.

Model discovery resolves each provider's list-models endpoint into flat ModelInfo {id, label, reasoning}; reasoning is read from the response where the provider says so (Anthropic capabilities.effort, Google thinking flag, OpenRouter supported_efforts) and otherwise inferred from a model-ID pattern (OpenAI o[0-9]/gpt-5 excluding -chat, Groq gpt-oss, xAI grok-4.5, Mistral small/medium).

DeepSeek and openai-compatible are deliberately left with no reasoning-effort control (DeepSeek's contract unconfirmed, self-hosted servers have no single shape), so the app never offers a control that silently does nothing on some servers.

The list-models pagination cursor is resolved as a URL against the base and rejected if it leaves the origin (resolveSameOrigin); this prevents a malicious cursor like '@evil.com/v1/models' parsing as userinfo and redirecting an API-key-bearing request to an attacker host.
fetchModels is cached per config id for MODELS_TTL_MS (1 hour) to make reopening the settings dialog instant; an explicit force refresh bypasses it, and it never attempts openai-compatible.

The system prompt teaches the model how an annotation schema is written (SCHEMA_FORMAT_DOC mirroring docs/annotation-schema.md §3) before showing one, so it reads an unfamiliar schema rather than pattern-matches; the format doc and the docs page must move together.

buildSystemPrompt is delivery-aware: when the paper arrives as extracted text it adds a rule warning the extraction is lossy (tables/figures/layout may be garbled, do not reconstruct illegible content), so the model does not confidently reconstruct a mangled table.

Every prompt rule pushes the model toward omitting a field rather than inventing one: ground values in the paper with no outside knowledge, omit fields the paper does not answer, quote a verbatim snippet of evidence for every value (or omit it), respect field types, and match enum options verbatim.

extractPdfText reconstructs reading-order lines by bucketing pdf.js items by baseline y and sorting each bucket by x (naive item-order join of a two-column paper is soup), normalizes to NFC after the join, and flags empty below EMPTY_CHAR_THRESHOLD (200 chars) as a scanned/image-only PDF that run() refuses to send.

parseAnswer is the trust boundary of the AI feature and never throws; it returns fields (accepted Suggestion[]), skipped (fields left empty with reasons), and rejected (refused suggestions kept and shown, because a silently dropped answer looks like the model said nothing).

extractObject tolerates a direct JSON parse, a ```json fence (with tag often missing/misspelled), and a balanced-brace scanner that knows about string literals/escapes (a regex cannot do this: a non-greedy match stops at the first '}' which usually sits inside a quoted evidence string).

Coercion bends only where there is exactly one honest reading: "2021" becomes number 2021, "true"/"True" becomes boolean, a case- or whitespace-off enum answer is snapped to its canonical option; everything else ("about 20", a value not in the enum, an empty string, a number for a string field) is rejected, never guessed.

Confidence outside 0..1 is dropped to null rather than clamped, because a model answering 95 may mean percent or a 1..100 scale; an empty string is not confidence 0 (Number('') is 0 inside the range).

resolvePath checks paths against the schema (not the current data) so the model may name an index that does not exist yet to record a further entry of a repeatable node; missing instances are created at apply time.

The maxUnboundedIndex option (MAX_UNBOUNDED_INDEX = 10000) is opt-in and only the LLM entry points opt in, because materializing every instance up to a named index makes a huge index an out-of-memory kill; applying the ceiling everywhere silently dropped real data in git/merge.ts.

Node names may contain /, [, ], or \ and are escaped with a backslash; a name with none of these characters must escape to itself for byte-compatibility, because canonical path strings are persisted (they key paper.equal marks and AI-mark keys).

isUnanswered matches validate.ts's empty notion for strings/numbers but booleans have their own rule: a boolean is offered unless already true (the AI can propose flipping to true, never to false, and never clears a ticked box), because the data model cannot represent an unanswered boolean.

useAiStore owns the AI flow as a phase state machine (setup → reading → calling → parsing → review → applied, with error reachable from network/extraction stages) and is kept separate from the main store; the UI invariant is nothing is sent until Start and nothing is written until Apply.

runFor is recorded when a run starts and apply reads it rather than the current selection, so a reply about paper A cannot be written onto paper B while the dialog, paper list, seat picker, and target picker stay usable in flight; a superseded run returns silently rather than publishing or narrating over the replacement.
At review every suggestion row is pre-ticked so the reviewer's job is to remove what is wrong (the direction that makes a careless click safe-ish); apply passes only the checked rows.

cancel aborts only and does not clear the controller slot (clearing it there made the run's own catch unable to tell an abort from a failure); the run clears the slot itself when it settles if it is still current.

verifyConfig saves the target first (the key must be stored before use), sends the smallest request that reliably answers ('Reply with OK'), uses a 2048-token budget below the real run, and distinguishes empty reply from budget-exhausted-on-reasoning via wasTruncated.

applyAiSuggestions is the only place model output reaches the project data and guarantees: it never overwrites the reviewer (a field answered since or a path that no longer resolves is skipped), the whole fill is one undo step, and a run that writes nothing leaves no trace.

applyAiSuggestions refuses at apply time if the project is multi-reviewer with no seat, the seat is Consolidation, it is a screening project, or the current paper/reviewer no longer matches the run's target — defending against retargeting rather than trusting the UI.
applyAiSuggestions usage comes from runFor (provider/model), not the current target selection, so switching the target between reply and Apply does not record the wrong provider/model.

aiMarks is session-only (lives beside the project, never serialized to disk) and marks fields the app filled that the reviewer has not looked at; useAiMark exposes the marked/confirm pair and confirmAiMark drops the mark.

AiUsageRecord is a persisted disclosure record appended to paper.aiUsage only when a fill actually changes something, recording provider, model, and the Apply timestamp; a wrong value there is a research-integrity problem.

LlmSettingsDialog enforces the key-invariant in the UI: an existing key is only ever hasKey (never shown/pre-filled), leaving the key box blank on an edit keeps the stored key, and Verify saves the target first because the key must be stored before anything can use it.

The settings dialog shows an honest runtime-specific notice: the key is encrypted in the OS keychain on desktop, but unencrypted in browser local storage on the web (why the desktop app is the supported path for AI annotation).

Switching provider resets the base URL, clears the model and reasoning effort (they belong to the old catalog), and clears the fetched model list; a reasoning-effort selector appears only for a model with a ReasoningProfile and a useEffect keeps reasoningEffort in step with the selected model.

ModelPicker is deliberately not ComboBox: the model field is a free-text input the reviewer can always type into (a catalog may be incomplete or unfetched), with a searchable dropdown and a red invalid flag judged only against a list actually fetched (an empty list means unknown, never invalid).

The preload bridge exposes five LLM calls (llmConfigs, saveLlmConfig, deleteLlmConfig, callLlm, abortLlm) with no way to read a stored API key back; abortLlm is a send (fire-and-forget), the rest are invokes.
callLlm generates a requestId so the renderer's AbortSignal (which cannot cross IPC) maps to a separate llm:abort send that the main process matches against the in-flight request.

The llm:call handler re-derives the configured origin and refuses to send the key unless the request URL scheme is http/https and matches the base protocol, and the origin matches exactly — preventing a compromised renderer posting the key to a host of its choosing, and avoiding a file: base authorizing any file: target.

The llm:call handler sends with net.fetch (no document origin, bypasses CORS that would block a renderer file:// fetch), uses redirect: 'error' to refuse redirects (following one would carry the substituted key — including unstripped provider-specific headers — past the origin check), and enforces a 10-minute timeout via an AbortController backed by an in-flight map.

encryptKey refuses rather than write the key in the clear when safeStorage is unavailable (e.g. Linux without a keyring), and publicConfigs strips the key and adds hasKey before returning configs to the renderer.

AI-assisted annotation is off by default for every project and unlocked only by a hidden per-session gesture (aiUnlocked, wired in Toolbar); a project can forbid it (config.ai: false always wins) but cannot turn it on by itself, and aiUnlocked is never persisted.
join appends a path to a base URL without duplicating what the user already typed, accepting http://host:1234, …/v1, or the full …/v1/chat/completions as the endpoint for openai-compatible.
